transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic today?
I took on this historical society fundraiser like I could do the whole thing myself. I started designing quilts, calling volunteers, making schedules, and promising deadlines I really couldn't meet.
During this time, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual to feel rested?

Yes. For a while I was only sleeping a few hours, but I'd wake up feeling ready to sew or start making phone calls. Now it's different—I either lie awake worrying, or I sleep late and still feel worn out.
Along with feeling worn out, have you been experiencing a persistently low, sad, or empty mood lately?
I'm not really sure. I know I've been worn out, but I wouldn't say I've noticed feeling sad or empty all the time.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you normally enjoy?
Yeah, I think so. I used to really enjoy checking on my garden and working on my own quilt entries, but lately I look at the fabric or the seed catalogs and just... don’t feel much of anything.
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
I don’t have a plan to hurt myself. But sometimes I think it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up, so nobody would have to deal with my mess anymore.
How much are these symptoms currently affecting your ability to manage everyday responsibilities, like work, chores, or taking care of yourself?

It’s affecting things quite a bit. My husband has taken over most of the household routines. I’ve also stopped keeping commitments with the historical society—I just couldn’t face the people who were waiting on me.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating, making decisions, or keeping your focus on things?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything specific with that.
